clue.text: A married Parisian is visiting city to find forgiveness

indicators.note: one piece visiting another goes inside it, so the French word sits within the city

parts.note: NY is short for New York, the city
est is French for 'is', as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: A married Frenchman in New York finds that others pardon him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parisian' signals French: 'is' in French is est.
explanation.definitionFit: An amnesty is an official pardon, a blanket act of forgiveness for offences.

clue.text: Regulator into lowering current a little in Missouri River

indicators.note: the moved word sits in the gap within the other letters

parts.note: MO is the postal abbreviation for Missouri

indicators.note: in a down answer lowering a letter moves it further down the word
a little means just one place, not far

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A regulator lowers a current a little as it flows into the Missouri River.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lowering ... a little' drops the I of INTO by one place, making NITO; in a down answer lower means later.
explanation.definitionFit: A monitor watches and controls a process, acting as a regulator or overseer.

clue.text: Lay journalist receiving honour

indicators.note: receiving means taking something in, so the honour goes inside

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the crossword journalist
MBE (Member of the Order of the British Empire) is a British honour

explanation.surface: A non-specialist journalist is awarded an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay' looks like an adjective (non-professional); it is the verb to set in place.
explanation.definitionFit: To embed something is to lay or fix it firmly within a surrounding mass.

clue.text: Time with au pair or char, occasionally making pudding

indicators.note: occasionally means every other letter is taken, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Spending time with the au pair or the cleaner, sometimes making a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: A char is a British cleaning lady (charwoman).
explanation.definitionFit: Tapioca is a starchy pudding made from cassava pearls cooked in milk.

clue.text: Failed drug test, inconclusive for tramps

indicators.note: something failed has gone wrong, so the letters are thrown into disorder
without a conclusion, the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: An athlete's failed drug test was inconclusive, a story about tramps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inconclusive' cuts TEST to TES; DRUG and TES are shuffled together by 'Failed'.
explanation.definitionFit: To tramp and to trudge are synonyms: both mean walking heavily and wearily.

clue.text: Religious education class is key once more

parts.note: RE is the school subject Religious Education
a type is a class or kind

explanation.surface: A school RE lesson is the key subject yet again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'class' looks like a school lesson; it means a kind. 'key' is to type.
explanation.definitionFit: To key text is to type it, so keying it again is retyping.

clue.text: Liberal MP is bad — without question, a disappointment.

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the rearranged letters surround the question
liberal means free, so the letters are treated freely and rearranged

explanation.surface: A Liberal MP is poor, unquestionably, and a letdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' gives DAMPSIB; 'without' is the old sense outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: A damp squib is a firework that fails to go off, and so any event that disappoints.

clue.text: Style to seduce using chatline essentially, instead of clubs

indicators.note: one piece goes in place of the other

parts.note: to entice is to lure or seduce
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

indicators.note: essentially means at its core, so the middle letters are taken

explanation.surface: A playboy's style of seduction via a chatline rather than nightclubs.
explanation.walkthrough: TL from chatline replaces C in ENTICE.
explanation.definitionFit: To entitle someone is to give them a title, to style or name them.

clue.text: Serious complaint originally brought up by our corporal in New Guinea

indicators.note: originally means at the origin, so each word's first letter
the corporal is placed in among the other letters
new means made afresh, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: CPL is the abbreviation for corporal

explanation.surface: A serious illness is raised by a corporal serving in New Guinea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' gives NIAGUE, split after its second letter by the corporal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bubonic plague is a deadly disease, so a grave illness.

clue.text: Stop cakes turning

indicators.note: turning round means the word for cakes is read backwards

parts.note: buns are small sweet cakes

explanation.surface: An instruction to stop the cakes from turning in the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses BUNS.
explanation.definitionFit: To snub originally meant to check or halt abruptly, as a rope is snubbed round a post; now a rebuff.

clue.text: Dwarf planet absorbing odd bits of meteor mass — astronaut's opening tinned food?

indicators.note: a piece absorbing others takes them inside itself

parts.note: Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters, first, third and fifth, are kept

parts.note: M is the symbol for mass in physics

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Pluto soaks up a meteor's mass as an astronaut opens a tin of food in space.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: plum tomatoes are often sold tinned.
explanation.definitionFit: Plum tomatoes are an oval variety, very commonly sold in cans, so they are an example of canned produce.

clue.text: Film company boss joining impresario on vacation

parts.note: a boss is a raised knob or stud on a surface

indicators.note: a word on vacation is emptied, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A film company's boss teams up with a theatrical impresario who is away on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' misleads as a manager; here it is a decorative knob.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio is a firm that makes films, as in the big Hollywood studios.

clue.text: Rival poet is performing work at the start

indicators.note: the work goes at the start, before the rest

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a musical work

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters are put through their paces into a new order

explanation.surface: A competing poet performs his work at the opening of the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performing' rearranges POET IS into POSITE.
explanation.definitionFit: An opposite, as in one's opposite number, is a counterpart on the other side, a competitor.

clue.text: Newspaper felt cutting photo could be sensible

indicators.note: pieces cutting a word split it open and sit inside it

parts.note: pic is a casual word for a photo
a rag is a low-quality newspaper
mat as a verb means to felt, to tangle fibres into a dense mass

explanation.surface: A newspaper decided that cropping a photograph would be the wise course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'felt' looks like a verb of feeling; it is the matted fabric sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A pragmatic approach is a practical, level-headed one, guided by what works.

clue.text: Nintendo ports a game over partially — it moves slowly

indicators.note: over means turned over, read backwards in a down answer
partially means only part of the words is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Nintendo ports a game over, only partly, and the result runs sluggishly.
explanation.walkthrough: The run DOPORTSAG inside the words, read backwards via 'over', gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A gastropod is a snail or slug, creatures famous for slowness.

clue.text: Cover song with verse in the middle

indicators.note: the verse letter is placed in the middle of the song

parts.note: a duet is a song for two voices

explanation.surface: A cover version of a song with a verse placed halfway through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover' suggests a cover version of a song; it is bedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A duvet is a quilted bed covering, a continental quilt.

clue.text: Hack making computer's first operating system stall

indicators.note: the first letter of computer is made into the operating system, swapping one for the other

parts.note: to hack in football is to kick an opponent

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A hacker's attack causes a computer's operating system to stall.
explanation.walkthrough: In KICK the first C (from 'computer's first') is changed to OS. 'Hack' and 'stall' read as computing terms.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiosk is a small booth or stand selling newspapers or snacks, a stall.

clue.text: Great memes in Twitch

indicators.note: to twitch is to jerk about, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Praise for the memes posted on the Twitch streaming platform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twitch' looks like the streaming site; as a verb it rearranges MEMES IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Immense means vast or enormous, which is great in size.

clue.text: Craft putting stoat's tail on pelt stole

indicators.note: the tail letter is put on the end of the rest

parts.note: to pelt along is to go at speed
a boa is a long scarf or stole of feathers or fur

indicators.note: a tail is the last letter of a word

explanation.surface: A fur stole is made by attaching a stoat's tail to its pelt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pelt' and 'stole' read as furs; they are a verb of rapid movement and a scarf.
explanation.definitionFit: A speedboat is a fast motorboat, a type of watercraft.

clue.text: Phone company taking in six pounds on executive toy — ultimately, it's a bad look?

indicators.note: taking in means holding inside, so the rest goes within

parts.note: EE is a British mobile phone network

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
L (from Latin libra) stands for pounds
E is the abbreviation for executive

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter

explanation.surface: A phone company spends six pounds on an office desk toy, which looks bad.
explanation.walkthrough: EE holds VILEY. The question mark flags the playful definition: a malevolent glance said to cast a curse.
explanation.definitionFit: The evil eye is a malicious gaze believed to bring harm, literally a baleful glance.

clue.text: Free love at sea, following sailors

indicators.note: the rearranged word follows the sailors

parts.note: ABs, able seamen, are sailors

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Sailors enjoying free love while out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' reorders LOVE as OLVE. 'Free' looks like an adjective; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To absolve is to release from guilt or obligation, to set free.

clue.text: Lob extremely deficient paint all over the place, one lacking pigment

indicators.note: all over the place means scattered in disorder, so the letters are mixed
deficient at the extremes, so the word loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Throwing paint about clumsily, splashing it everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Trimming PAINT leaves AIN, shuffled with LOB.
explanation.definitionFit: An albino is a person or animal born without normal skin and hair colouring.

clue.text: Protection from turbulent bull market — almost losing grand

indicators.note: turbulent means agitated and disordered, so the letters are churned
losing a letter means it is removed
almost the whole word, so the last letter goes

parts.note: K, for kilo (a thousand), is slang for a grand

explanation.surface: Seeking a safe haven from a volatile bull market that has nearly lost a thousand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims MARKET to MARKE, and losing K leaves MARE; 'turbulent' shuffles BULL and MARE.
explanation.definitionFit: An umbrella gives shelter from rain, and figuratively any protective cover.

clue.text: Demand from current, reported growth

parts.note: in means current or fashionable

indicators.note: reported means as heard out loud, so the word is given by its sound

parts.note: a cyst is an abnormal growth

explanation.surface: Requesting news from the latest reports on a growth.
explanation.walkthrough: CYST is said aloud and entered as SIST.
explanation.definitionFit: To insist is to demand firmly, refusing to take no for an answer.

clue.text: Hardly any name dropping's entertaining

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so the name goes inside

parts.note: scat is animal droppings, and the 's means is

explanation.surface: Name-dropping is barely amusing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'name dropping' reads as one idea; split it: dropping (SCAT) is entertaining N.
explanation.definitionFit: Scant means barely sufficient, as in scant attention, so very little.

clue.text: Stupidity of Italy having stripped tops off — kept fit inside

parts.note: I is the international vehicle code for Italy

indicators.note: these letters go inside the naked word

parts.note: stripped means naked, nude

indicators.note: each word loses its top, its first letter

explanation.surface: An Italian stripped off, keeping fit, which looked foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tops off' applies to both words, leaving EPTIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Ineptitude is lack of skill or sense, clumsy foolishness.

clue.text: Join forces every year

parts.note: all means every

explanation.surface: Nations team up together every year.
explanation.definitionFit: To ally is to unite with another side, forming an alliance.

clue.text: You would go cross-eyed looking at this strangely worded page

definitions.text: You would go cross-eyed looking at this

indicators.note: strangely means in an odd way, so the letters are arranged oddly

explanation.surface: A page so oddly worded that reading it makes you go cross-eyed.
explanation.walkthrough: A drop on the end of one's nose is so close one goes cross-eyed peering at it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dewdrop is also a drip hanging from the nose, which one sees only by crossing the eyes.

clue.text: Lightly touch on that woman's achievement first

indicators.note: the achievement comes first in the answer

parts.note: a feat is a notable achievement
her is the possessive meaning that woman's

explanation.surface: Delicately mentioning that woman's accomplishment before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: To feather is to brush gently, as with a feather, for instance a light touch on brakes or oars.
